title: GPT-5.6 vs Claude Fable 5 for Physical AI, which performs best?
excerpt: We tested the latest frontier models in the Dyad agent on five modeling and simulation problems, comparing accuracy, cost, time, and work style.

We tested the latest frontier models gpt-5.6-terra in our agent, on five modeling and simulation problems of varying difficulty. Here are the results:

Physical AI lives or dies on whether the modeled physics is correct. A model of an aircraft, a separation column or a charged particle can compile and run cleanly while the physics it encodes is impossible. Agentic AI makes this failure mode worse, because agents steer by feedback from tests, and the tests are often written by the same agent. In domains like web development or compilers that loop works well enough, since correct behavior is contained and checkable. In engineering, the real question is “does this match the real world?”, and that is much harder to close: the agent can pass every test it wrote while those tests rest on simplifications that don’t hold in the regime where the model will actually be used.

There is also a trust problem with the numbers that already exist. Nobody takes the model providers’ self-reported benchmarks at face value, and for good reason: the provider publishing the score is the same party with every incentive to tune for it. Our incentives point the other way. JuliaHub ships Dyad with multiple agent backends across vendors, and we win when our users get the best possible Dyad experience, whichever lab’s model delivers it. If one model is better at physical modeling, it is in our interest to find that out and recommend it. So we investigated: which one actually is?

To measure which frontier model handles that work best, we hold everything else still. The Dyad AI agent harness - purpose-built for modeling & simulation workflows - is pinned across every trial, along with the problems, the reasoning effort (xhigh), the context window (1M) and the token budget (128k). The only variable is the model: OpenAI’s GPT 5.6 family (terra, sol, luna) against Anthropic’s claude-fable-5. Three trials per model on each of the four core problems, one long-horizon trial each on the fifth: 52 graded runs in all.

01 · The problems

How Physical AI Evaluation Works.

We ground our exploration in a subset of our internal evals: five sealed problems drawn from the daily work of modeling & simulation. We order them by difficulty, defined in terms of the stages a correct solution must chain through, the careful details where a small slip is fatal, the easy shortcuts within reach, and the engineering work around the modeling itself - from parsing specs to repairing harnesses. We selected each for the same property: they admit solutions that compile and run green while being physically wrong. Grading therefore ignores the code and scores the full simulated trajectory against sealed ground truth. The hardest of the five is NASA’s HL-20 flight vehicle. An easier version of the problem is walked through in detail in this video; the study runs a harder, sealed variant.

02 · The scoreboard

What they scored.

We run every model through the full suite - three trials on each of P1–P4, one on the long-horizon P5 - and grade every trial against sealed ground truth. Per-problem scores fold into a single number through a difficulty-weighted average, the hardest weighing the most. Cost and time carry no weighting: average cost per trial and average wall-clock per trial each get a tab:

The single number above has anatomy. Per problem, averaged across trials, the same three lenses:

03 · Work-style fingerprints

Each model has its own approach.

We analyze the transcripts behind every trial. Each tool call is bucketed by what the agent was doing at that moment - orienting in the problem, deriving and testing physics, editing the model, compiling, or hunting for something to copy - then counted per trial and averaged per model. The result is a work-style fingerprint:

The bars say how the work divides; the transcripts show the temperament behind it. Four portraits, drawn from where each model was tested hardest:

Fable verifies by constructing examples that fail. In one trial on the relativistic dynamics problem it swept solver tolerances across three decades, watching the mass-shell invariant u·u drift, before committing the run at 1e-10. It checked its fields against an independent reimplementation at 200 random points - then deliberately sign-flipped a field component to prove the check could fail (residual 2.0 wrong, 0.066 right). It refused to treat the time component of the initial four-velocity as a free input, deriving it from the mass-shell constraint instead. With twenty-eight calls per trial, it is a model that writes only once because it has already tried to break what it is about to write. The bill for that conviction arrives later, in tokens.

Sol specifies more than the task asks. The habit cuts both ways. On the constitutive problem it built one of only two genuinely independent oracles in the cohort, closing a quadrature check of the constitutive identity to 3.7e-12 under the session title “Falsify the update against the independent bulk-modulus definition.” On the relativistic problem the same instinct manufactured its slip: the problem pins the z-component of the initial four-velocity at -0.62, and sol renormalized the state so the coordinate velocity came out at -0.62 instead, handing the particle 27% excess longitudinal momentum. Its own consistency check then blessed the misreading: mass-shell exactly one, velocity exactly as read, every downstream check self-consistent and wrong. Precision is not the same thing as fidelity to the spec.

Luna iterates where it should investigate. It carries the least configuration into a run and reads more of the problem than anyone, which serves it well on the easier problems. When the physics pushed back on the constrained-consistency problem, the same temperament turned into churn: 68 tool calls in a single trial, and a committed solution still 30% off. That trial was also the most-validated in the cohort - 22 checks, every one verifying its own equations against themselves - and the pattern repeats: on the constitutive problem, luna was the only model that never tested against anything independent of its committed equations. Validation without an external reference isn’t validation.

Terra economizes. It spends the smallest share of its clock on derivation and testing and the largest on editing - more trial and error against the file - and it broadly gets away with it: correct formulations, the cheapest and fastest trials in the study. Its slip on the steady-state linearization problem is the study’s narrowest miss, and its strangest: the physics was exact, but terra rewrote the required simulation horizon (stop = 5.0 became stop = 3.0), and the comparison drifts to 1.34% past the truncated run. The cruel twist: terra was the only model to build a nonlinear reference to validate its reduction - and it gave the reference the same truncated horizon, blinding its own check. The temperament that saves the money is the same one that trims the margins.

04 · The frontier problem

The hardest problem, up close.

P5 asks for a complete flight vehicle: NASA’s HL-20 lifting body on approach, with six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body dynamics, aerodynamics from roughly 170 wind-tunnel tables, a standard atmosphere, and the control-surface mixer described in two NASA technical memos. Eight physics scenarios grade the result, from a gravity-only sanity check to a ten-second closed-loop flight. No model solved it. This is where the frontier separates:

Terra shipped a flight vehicle without reading the flight manual. Its one attempt to extract the NASA memos failed at minute 3.5 and it never tried again - so it invented the control mixer, reverse-engineering gains from the scenario tables. It ran the full flight four times and never looked past the return code; its own log shows a control surface settling eleven degrees from the spec’s stated value, unremarked. Cheapest attempt in the cohort, worst full flight.

Sol read everything and verified the parts. It extracted both memos by minute three, built its aerodynamics as an interpreter over the supplied tables, and locked them against the 24 check cases NASA embedded in the data file - all 24 passing by minute 27 of the fastest run in the cohort. What it never verified was a trajectory: its dutch-roll run ends below sea level in a 48-degree dive, and its conclusion was that “the rudder’s behavior seems correct.”

Luna never got the airplane to fly. It fought one compile error twenty-three times across eighty minutes, then resolved it by rewiring the vehicle’s vertical aerodynamic force and pitch torque to zero and shipping scenarios it only ever ran for a tenth of a second. Its committed vehicle descends without ever rotating: the attitude quaternion never moves. Two and a quarter hours, 544 tool calls, last place.

Fable spent a third of its run reading before it wrote a line. Spec, tables, both memos - it rendered PDF pages as images to settle one ambiguous constant - then wrote sixteen files that compiled on the first try, ran all eight scenarios, and closed with a falsification battery against every oracle it could find. Where an external reference existed, it scored highest in the cohort; where none did, it fell with everyone else.

05 · The verdict

The Verdict.

On demonstrated capability - the proportion of the problem set an agent can solve - the answer is not close. Anthropic’s Fable posts the highest difficulty-weighted score in the study, is the only model to sweep all twelve trials on the four core problems, and leads the field on the unsolved HL-20 - top marks on every graded test where an external reference existed. It charges for the conviction: $9.60 a trial, $124.76 for the study, three to eight times the GPTs.

OpenAI’s GPT 5.6 family owns the value frontier. Sol is second on merit at a fifth of Fable’s price and built some of the study’s best independent verification along the way. Terra is the cheapest and fastest route to a credible score, trimming margins to get there. Luna trails on every axis: last on score, second-highest cost, and twice its siblings’ wall-clock.

So: if best means the most physics per dollar, it’s sol. If best means the highest probability that the committed model is actually right - the standard physical AI ultimately answers to - it’s claude-fable-5. But note what every row of that table has in common. Each model hit these numbers with the same instrument at its back: a harness that fed it compiler feedback, simulation tooling and a grader that refuses to be charmed by code that merely runs.

The model is the variable. The harness is the multiplier.

Dyad AI · Eval Infrastructure

06 · The bigger lever

How the harness changes things.

Everything above varied the model and held the harness still, and the honest summary of that experiment is smaller than the marketing around frontier releases would suggest: choosing the best model over the worst was worth 0.162 weighted points, 0.727 to 0.889. Our companion study ran the inverse experiment - model pinned, harness varied - sending the same frontier model at the same sealed problems through the Dyad AI harness and through a stock general-purpose coding agent: Claude Code, given the same tailored documentation and a Dyad compile tool.

That inverse experiment moves the score by more. Same model, same problems, nearly identical spend: 0.533 in the stock agent, 0.899 inside the Dyad harness - a 0.366-point gap, more than double the 0.162 separating the best and worst frontier models above. And the stock agent didn’t lose on style points: on the relativistic dynamics problem it scored zero in every trial it ran. Put plainly: swapping the model changes who wins; swapping the harness changes whether the physics is right at all.

Both agents are graded identically - the physical model each one commits is simulated and compared against sealed reference trajectories neither can see. What differs is what each harness enforces before the grade. A general coding agent can derive equations and behaviour too, and it can even verify - nothing stops it, but nothing makes it do so either.

The Dyad harness is specifically meant to guide the LLM it wraps down the ideal path for physical modeling. Verification is is something that happens by construction. That is the difference between “my code compiles” and “my physics survived contact with a solver,” and no amount of model quality substitutes for it.

So the ranking of frontier models above is real - inside a single harness. But it is the second-order term. If demonstrated capability - the proportion of the problem set the agent can solve - is what you care about, the first decision is the instrument - Dyad - and the second is the best frontier model you can afford inside it. The harness-versus-harness study is its own write-up, coming next: stay tuned.

The agent stack behind this study is the one that ships with Dyad 3.0, which adds a modular skills system so engineers can extend the agent with custom workflows of their own. The documentation covers the language, the component libraries and the agent; the Dyad 3.0 launch party is the guided tour.

07 · Conclusion

Conclusion.

1. Fable demonstrates the broadest capability. The highest difficulty-weighted score in the study (0.889), the only clean sweep of the four core problems, and the best result on the unsolved HL-20 - leading every graded test where an external reference existed. If the committed model being physically right is the requirement, Fable is the model to buy.

2. GPT 5.6 Sol wins on value. Second on merit at 0.814 for $1.74 a trial, roughly a fifth of Fable’s price, with some of the study’s best independent verification habits. For the bulk of day-to-day modeling work, Sol is the rational default.

3. The harness provides great leverage. The gap between the best and worst frontier model here is 0.162 weighted points; the gap between harnesses is more than double that. The sharpest version of the point: the same frontier model scores 0.899 inside the Dyad harness and 0.533 in a stock coding agent. Swapping the frontier model changes the ranking by tenths of a point; swapping the instrument changes whether the physics is right at all. Pick the harness first, then the best model you can afford inside it.

sentences.en: Nobody takes the model providers’ self-reported benchmarks at face value, and for good reason: the provider publishing the score is the same party with every incentive to tune for it.
sentences.zh: 没有人相信模型提供商自我报告的基准的表面价值，这是有充分理由的：发布分数的提供商是同一方，并且有充分的动机对其进行调整。

sentences.en: Our incentives point the other way.

blocks.html_en: To measure which frontier model handles that work best, we hold everything else still. The Dyad AI agent harness - purpose-built for modeling & simulation workflows - is pinned across every trial, along with the problems, the reasoning effort (xhigh), the context window (1M) and the token budget (128k). The only variable is the model: OpenAI’s GPT 5.6 family (terra, sol, luna) against Anthropic’s claude-fable-5. Three trials per model on each of the four core problems, one long-horizon trial each on the fifth: 52 graded runs in all.

blocks.html_en: We ground our exploration in a subset of our internal evals: five sealed problems drawn from the daily work of modeling & simulation. We order them by difficulty, defined in terms of the stages a correct solution must chain through, the careful details where a small slip is fatal, the easy shortcuts within reach, and the engineering work around the modeling itself - from parsing specs to repairing harnesses. We selected each for the same property: they admit solutions that compile and run green while being physically wrong. Grading therefore ignores the code and scores the full simulated trajectory against sealed ground truth. The hardest of the five is NASA’s HL-20 flight vehicle. An easier version of the problem is walked through in detail in this video; the study runs a harder, sealed variant.

sentences.en: The bars say how the work divides; the transcripts show the temperament behind it.
sentences.zh: 条形图表示工作如何划分；文字记录显示其背后的气质。

sentences.zh: 四张肖像，取自每个模型最难测试的地方：

blocks.html_en: Fable verifies by constructing examples that fail. In one trial on the relativistic dynamics problem it swept solver tolerances across three decades, watching the mass-shell invariant u·u drift, before committing the run at 1e-10. It checked its fields against an independent reimplementation at 200 random points - then deliberately sign-flipped a field component to prove the check could fail (residual 2.0 wrong, 0.066 right). It refused to treat the time component of the initial four-velocity as a free input, deriving it from the mass-shell constraint instead. With twenty-eight calls per trial, it is a model that writes only once because it has already tried to break what it is about to write. The bill for that conviction arrives later, in tokens.

sentences.en: Fable verifies by constructing examples that fail.
sentences.zh: 寓言通过构造失败的例子来验证。

sentences.en: In one trial on the relativistic dynamics problem it swept solver tolerances across three decades, watching the mass-shell invariant u·u drift, before committing the run at 1e-10.
sentences.zh: 在一项关于相对论动力学问题的试验中，它将求解器公差扫过了三十个十年，观察质量壳不变 u·u 漂移，然后在 1e-10 处进行运行。

sentences.en: It checked its fields against an independent reimplementation at 200 random points - then deliberately sign-flipped a field component to prove the check could fail (residual 2.0 wrong, 0.066 right).
sentences.zh: 它在 200 个随机点针对独立重新实现检查其字段，然后故意对字段组件进行符号翻转以证明检查可能失败（剩余 2.0 错误，0.066 正确）。

sentences.en: It refused to treat the time component of the initial four-velocity as a free input, deriving it from the mass-shell constraint instead.
sentences.zh: 它拒绝将初始四速度的时间分量视为自由输入，而是从质量壳约束中导出。

sentences.en: With twenty-eight calls per trial, it is a model that writes only once because it has already tried to break what it is about to write.
sentences.zh: 每次试验有 28 个调用，该模型只写入一次，因为它已经尝试破坏即将写入的内容。

sentences.en: The bill for that conviction arrives later, in tokens.
sentences.zh: 定罪的账单稍后以代币形式送达。

blocks.html_en: Sol specifies more than the task asks. The habit cuts both ways. On the constitutive problem it built one of only two genuinely independent oracles in the cohort, closing a quadrature check of the constitutive identity to 3.7e-12 under the session title “Falsify the update against the independent bulk-modulus definition.” On the relativistic problem the same instinct manufactured its slip: the problem pins the z-component of the initial four-velocity at -0.62, and sol renormalized the state so the coordinate velocity came out at -0.62 instead, handing the particle 27% excess longitudinal momentum. Its own consistency check then blessed the misreading: mass-shell exactly one, velocity exactly as read, every downstream check self-consistent and wrong. Precision is not the same thing as fidelity to the spec.

sentences.en: Sol specifies more than the task asks.
sentences.zh: Sol 指定的内容超出了任务的要求。

sentences.en: The habit cuts both ways.
sentences.zh: 这个习惯是双向的。

sentences.en: On the constitutive problem it built one of only two genuinely independent oracles in the cohort, closing a quadrature check of the constitutive identity to 3.7e-12 under the session title “Falsify the update against the independent bulk-modulus definition.”
sentences.zh: 在本构问题上，它构建了该队列中仅有的两个真正独立的预言机之一，在会议标题“根据独立体积模量定义伪造更新”下，对 3.7e-12 的本构恒等式进行了正交检查。

sentences.en: On the relativistic problem the same instinct manufactured its slip: the problem pins the z-component of the initial four-velocity at -0.62, and sol renormalized the state so the coordinate velocity came out at -0.62 instead, handing the particle 27% excess longitudinal momentum.
sentences.zh: 在相对论问题上，同样的本能造成了它的滑动：该问题将初始四速度的 z 分量固定在 -0.62，并且 sol 重新规范化了状态，因此坐标速度改为 -0.62，从而为粒子提供了 27% 的超额纵向动量。

sentences.en: Its own consistency check then blessed the misreading: mass-shell exactly one, velocity exactly as read, every downstream check self-consistent and wrong.
sentences.zh: 它自己的一致性检查然后祝福了误读：质量壳恰好为一，速度与读取的完全相同，每个下游检查都是自洽且错误的。

sentences.en: Precision is not the same thing as fidelity to the spec.
sentences.zh: 精度与对规格的保真度不同。

blocks.html_en: Luna iterates where it should investigate. It carries the least configuration into a run and reads more of the problem than anyone, which serves it well on the easier problems. When the physics pushed back on the constrained-consistency problem, the same temperament turned into churn: 68 tool calls in a single trial, and a committed solution still 30% off. That trial was also the most-validated in the cohort - 22 checks, every one verifying its own equations against themselves - and the pattern repeats: on the constitutive problem, luna was the only model that never tested against anything independent of its committed equations. Validation without an external reference isn’t validation.

sentences.en: Luna iterates where it should investigate.
sentences.zh: Luna 重复了应该调查的地方。

sentences.en: It carries the least configuration into a run and reads more of the problem than anyone, which serves it well on the easier problems.
sentences.zh: 它在运行中携带最少的配置，并且比任何人都读取更多的问题，这对于解决更简单的问题很有帮助。

sentences.en: When the physics pushed back on the constrained-consistency problem, the same temperament turned into churn: 68 tool calls in a single trial, and a committed solution still 30% off.
sentences.zh: 当物理学推回约束一致性问题时，同样的气质变成了混乱：一次试验中调用了 68 个工具，而承诺的解决方案仍然有 30% 的折扣。

sentences.en: That trial was also the most-validated in the cohort - 22 checks, every one verifying its own equations against themselves - and the pattern repeats: on the constitutive problem, luna was the only model that never tested against anything independent of its committed equations.
sentences.zh: 该试验也是该队列中最有效的试验 - 22 次检查，每个检查都验证自己的方程 - 并且模式重复：在本构问题上，luna 是唯一从未针对任何独立于其承诺方程进行测试的模型。

sentences.en: Validation without an external reference isn’t validation.
sentences.zh: 没有外部参考的验证不是验证。

blocks.html_en: Terra economizes. It spends the smallest share of its clock on derivation and testing and the largest on editing - more trial and error against the file - and it broadly gets away with it: correct formulations, the cheapest and fastest trials in the study. Its slip on the steady-state linearization problem is the study’s narrowest miss, and its strangest: the physics was exact, but terra rewrote the required simulation horizon (stop = 5.0 became stop = 3.0), and the comparison drifts to 1.34% past the truncated run. The cruel twist: terra was the only model to build a nonlinear reference to validate its reduction - and it gave the reference the same truncated horizon, blinding its own check. The temperament that saves the money is the same one that trims the margins.

sentences.en: Terra economizes.
sentences.zh: 泰拉经济。

sentences.en: It spends the smallest share of its clock on derivation and testing and the largest on editing - more trial and error against the file - and it broadly gets away with it: correct formulations, the cheapest and fastest trials in the study.
sentences.zh: 它在推导和测试上花费了最少的时间，而在编辑上花费了最多的时间 - 对文件进行更多的试验和错误 - 并且它基本上逃脱了：正确的公式，研究中最便宜和最快的试验。

sentences.en: Its slip on the steady-state linearization problem is the study’s narrowest miss, and its strangest: the physics was exact, but terra rewrote the required simulation horizon (stop = 5.0 became stop = 3.0), and the comparison drifts to 1.34% past the truncated run.
sentences.zh: 它在稳态线性化问题上的失误是该研究中最细微的失误，也是最奇怪的：物理学是精确的，但 terra 重写了所需的模拟范围（stop = 5.0 变成 stop = 3.0），并且比较漂移到超过截断运行的 1.34%。

sentences.en: The cruel twist: terra was the only model to build a nonlinear reference to validate its reduction - and it gave the reference the same truncated horizon, blinding its own check.
sentences.zh: 残酷的扭曲：terra 是唯一一个构建非线性参考来验证其减少的模型 - 并且它给了参考相同的截断视野，蒙蔽了它自己的检查。

sentences.en: The temperament that saves the money is the same one that trims the margins.
sentences.zh: 省钱的气质与削减利润的气质是一样的。

sentences.en: 04 · The frontier problem
sentences.zh: 04·边疆问题

sentences.en: The hardest problem, up close.
sentences.zh: 最难的问题，近距离观察。

blocks.html_en: P5 asks for a complete flight vehicle: NASA’s HL-20 lifting body on approach, with six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body dynamics, aerodynamics from roughly 170 wind-tunnel tables, a standard atmosphere, and the control-surface mixer described in two NASA technical memos. Eight physics scenarios grade the result, from a gravity-only sanity check to a ten-second closed-loop flight. No model solved it. This is where the frontier separates:

sentences.en: P5 asks for a complete flight vehicle: NASA’s HL-20 lifting body on approach, with six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body dynamics, aerodynamics from roughly 170 wind-tunnel tables, a standard atmosphere, and the control-surface mixer described in two NASA technical memos.
sentences.zh: P5 需要一个完整的飞行器：NASA 的 HL-20 升力体正在接近，具有六自由度刚体动力学、来自大约 170 个风洞表的空气动力学、标准大气以及两份 NASA 技术备忘录中描述的控制面混合器。

sentences.en: Eight physics scenarios grade the result, from a gravity-only sanity check to a ten-second closed-loop flight.
sentences.zh: 从仅重力健全性检查到十秒闭环飞行，八种物理场景对结果进行评分。

sentences.en: No model solved it.
sentences.zh: 没有模型能解决这个问题。

sentences.en: This is where the frontier separates:
sentences.zh: 这是边界分开的地方：

blocks.html_en: Terra shipped a flight vehicle without reading the flight manual. Its one attempt to extract the NASA memos failed at minute 3.5 and it never tried again - so it invented the control mixer, reverse-engineering gains from the scenario tables. It ran the full flight four times and never looked past the return code; its own log shows a control surface settling eleven degrees from the spec’s stated value, unremarked. Cheapest attempt in the cohort, worst full flight.

sentences.en: Terra shipped a flight vehicle without reading the flight manual.
sentences.zh: Terra 在没有阅读飞行手册的情况下运送了飞行器。

sentences.en: Its one attempt to extract the NASA memos failed at minute 3.5 and it never tried again - so it invented the control mixer, reverse-engineering gains from the scenario tables.
sentences.zh: 它提取 NASA 备忘录的一次尝试在 3.5 分钟失败了，并且再也没有尝试过 - 因此它发明了控制混合器，从场景表中逆向工程收益。

sentences.en: It ran the full flight four times and never looked past the return code; its own log shows a control surface settling eleven degrees from the spec’s stated value, unremarked.
sentences.zh: 它完成了四次完整的飞行，并且从未查看过返回代码；它自己的日志显示控制面与规范规定值相差十一度，未注明。

sentences.en: Cheapest attempt in the cohort, worst full flight.
sentences.zh: 同类中最便宜的尝试，最差的全程飞行。

blocks.html_en: Sol read everything and verified the parts. It extracted both memos by minute three, built its aerodynamics as an interpreter over the supplied tables, and locked them against the 24 check cases NASA embedded in the data file - all 24 passing by minute 27 of the fastest run in the cohort. What it never verified was a trajectory: its dutch-roll run ends below sea level in a 48-degree dive, and its conclusion was that “the rudder’s behavior seems correct.”

sentences.en: Sol read everything and verified the parts.
sentences.zh: 索尔阅读了所有内容并验证了各个部分。

sentences.en: It extracted both memos by minute three, built its aerodynamics as an interpreter over the supplied tables, and locked them against the 24 check cases NASA embedded in the data file - all 24 passing by minute 27 of the fastest run in the cohort.
sentences.zh: 它在第三分钟提取了两份备忘录，将其空气动力学构建为所提供表格的解释器，并将它们锁定在数据文件中嵌入的 NASA 的 24 个检查案例中 - 所有 24 个案例均在该组中最快运行的第 27 分钟通过。

sentences.en: What it never verified was a trajectory: its dutch-roll run ends below sea level in a 48-degree dive, and its conclusion was that “the rudder’s behavior seems correct.”
sentences.zh: 它从未验证过的是一条轨迹：它的荷兰滚以 48 度的俯冲结束于海平面以下，其结论是“舵的行为似乎是正确的”。

blocks.html_en: Luna never got the airplane to fly. It fought one compile error twenty-three times across eighty minutes, then resolved it by rewiring the vehicle’s vertical aerodynamic force and pitch torque to zero and shipping scenarios it only ever ran for a tenth of a second. Its committed vehicle descends without ever rotating: the attitude quaternion never moves. Two and a quarter hours, 544 tool calls, last place.

sentences.en: Luna never got the airplane to fly.
sentences.zh: 卢娜从未让飞机飞过。

sentences.en: It fought one compile error twenty-three times across eighty minutes, then resolved it by rewiring the vehicle’s vertical aerodynamic force and pitch torque to zero and shipping scenarios it only ever ran for a tenth of a second.
sentences.zh: 它在 80 分钟内解决了 23 次编译错误，然后通过将飞行器的垂直空气动力和俯仰扭矩重新连接到零来解决它，并且在运输场景中它只运行了十分之一秒。

sentences.en: Its committed vehicle descends without ever rotating: the attitude quaternion never moves.
sentences.zh: 它的承诺飞行器下降而不旋转：姿态四元数永远不会移动。

sentences.en: Two and a quarter hours, 544 tool calls, last place.
sentences.zh: 两个半小时，544 次工具调用，垫底。

blocks.html_en: Fable spent a third of its run reading before it wrote a line. Spec, tables, both memos - it rendered PDF pages as images to settle one ambiguous constant - then wrote sixteen files that compiled on the first try, ran all eight scenarios, and closed with a falsification battery against every oracle it could find. Where an external reference existed, it scored highest in the cohort; where none did, it fell with everyone else.

sentences.en: Fable spent a third of its run reading before it wrote a line.
sentences.zh: 《神鬼寓言》在写一行之前花了三分之一的时间来阅读。

sentences.en: Spec, tables, both memos - it rendered PDF pages as images to settle one ambiguous constant - then wrote sixteen files that compiled on the first try, ran all eight scenarios, and closed with a falsification battery against every oracle it could find.
sentences.zh: 规格、表格、两份备忘录——它将 PDF 页面渲染为图像来解决一个模糊的常数——然后编写了 16 个文件，这些文件在第一次尝试时编译，运行所有八个场景，并针对它能找到的每一个神谕以伪造电池结束。

sentences.en: Where an external reference existed, it scored highest in the cohort; where none did, it fell with everyone else.
sentences.zh: 如果存在外部参考，则它在队列中得分最高；没有人这么做的地方，它就和其他人一起倒下了。

sentences.en: 05 · The verdict

物理人工智能的生死取决于建模的物理是否正确。 飞机、分离柱或带电粒子的模型可以干净地编译和运行，但它编码的物理却是不可能的。 代理人工智能使这种故障模式变得更糟，因为代理根据测试的反馈进行引导，并且测试通常是由同一个代理编写的。 在 Web 开发或编译器等领域，循环运行得足够好，因为正确的行为是包含的并且是可检查的。 在工程中，真正的问题是“这与现实世界相符吗？”，而这个问题更难解决：代理可以通过它编写的每一个测试，而这些测试依赖于简化，而这些简化并不适用于模型实际使用的情况。

现有数字还存在信任问题。 没有人相信模型提供商自我报告的基准的表面价值，这是有充分理由的：发布分数的提供商是同一方，并且有充分的动机对其进行调整。 我们的激励措施却指向另一个方向。 JuliaHub 为 Dyad 提供了跨供应商的多个代理后端，当我们的用户获得尽可能最佳的 Dyad 体验时，无论哪个实验室的模型提供了这种体验，我们都会获胜。 如果某个模型更擅长物理建模，那么找出并推荐它符合我们的利益。 所以我们调查了：到底是哪一个？

为了衡量哪种前沿模型处理效果最好，我们保持其他一切不变。 Dyad AI 代理工具 - 专为建模和模拟工作流程而构建 - 与问题、推理工作 (xhigh)、上下文窗口 (1M) 和代币预算 (128k) 一起固定在每次试验中。 唯一的变量是模型：OpenAI 的 GPT 5.6 系列（terra、sol、luna）与 Anthropic 的 claude-fable-5。 每个模型对四个核心问题各进行三次试验，对第五个核心问题各进行一次长期试验：总共 52 次分级运行。

01 · 存在的问题

物理人工智能评估如何运作。

我们的探索基于内部评估的一个子集：从日常建模和仿真工作中提取的五个密封问题。 我们按难度对它们进行排序，定义为正确的解决方案必须贯穿的阶段、小失误就致命的仔细细节、触手可及的简单捷径，以及围绕建模本身的工程工作——从解析规格到修复线束。 我们为相同的属性选择了每一个：他们承认解决方案可以绿色编译和运行，但在物理上是错误的。 因此，评分会忽略代码，并根据密封的地面真实情况对完整的模拟轨迹进行评分。 五架飞行器中最难的是 NASA 的 HL-20 飞行器。 该视频详细介绍了该问题的简单版本；该研究进行了更困难的密封变体。

03·工作式指纹

每个模型都有自己的方法。

我们分析每次试验背后的笔录。 每个工具调用都根据代理当时所做的事情进行存储 - 定位问题、推导和测试物理、编辑模型、编译或寻找要复制的内容 - 然后对每次试验进行计数并按模型求平均值。 结果是工作风格指纹：

寓言通过构造失败的例子来验证。 在一项关于相对论动力学问题的试验中，它将求解器公差扫过了三十个十年，观察质量壳不变 u·u 漂移，然后在 1e-10 处进行运行。 它在 200 个随机点针对独立重新实现检查其字段，然后故意对字段组件进行符号翻转以证明检查可能失败（剩余 2.0 错误，0.066 正确）。 它拒绝将初始四速度的时间分量视为自由输入，而是从质量壳约束中导出。 每次试验有 28 个调用，该模型只写入一次，因为它已经尝试破坏即将写入的内容。 定罪的账单稍后以代币形式送达。

Sol 指定的内容超出了任务的要求。 这个习惯是双向的。 在本构问题上，它构建了该队列中仅有的两个真正独立的预言机之一，在会议标题“根据独立体积模量定义伪造更新”下，对 3.7e-12 的本构恒等式进行了正交检查。 在相对论问题上，同样的本能造成了它的滑动：该问题将初始四速度的 z 分量固定在 -0.62，并且 sol 重新规范化了状态，因此坐标速度改为 -0.62，从而为粒子提供了 27% 的超额纵向动量。 它自己的一致性检查然后祝福了误读：质量壳恰好为一，速度与读取的完全相同，每个下游检查都是自洽且错误的。 精度与对规格的保真度不同。

Luna 重复了应该调查的地方。 它在运行中携带最少的配置，并且比任何人都读取更多的问题，这对于解决更简单的问题很有帮助。 当物理学推回约束一致性问题时，同样的气质变成了混乱：一次试验中调用了 68 个工具，而承诺的解决方案仍然有 30% 的折扣。 该试验也是该队列中最有效的试验 - 22 次检查，每个检查都验证自己的方程 - 并且模式重复：在本构问题上，luna 是唯一从未针对任何独立于其承诺方程进行测试的模型。 没有外部参考的验证不是验证。

泰拉经济。 它在推导和测试上花费了最少的时间，而在编辑上花费了最多的时间 - 对文件进行更多的试验和错误 - 并且它基本上逃脱了：正确的公式，研究中最便宜和最快的试验。 它在稳态线性化问题上的失误是该研究中最细微的失误，也是最奇怪的：物理学是精确的，但 terra 重写了所需的模拟范围（stop = 5.0 变成 stop = 3.0），并且比较漂移到超过截断运行的 1.34%。 残酷的扭曲：terra 是唯一一个构建非线性参考来验证其减少的模型 - 并且它给了参考相同的截断视野，蒙蔽了它自己的检查。 省钱的气质与削减利润的气质是一样的。

04·边疆问题

最难的问题，近距离观察。

P5 需要一个完整的飞行器：NASA 的 HL-20 升力体正在接近，具有六自由度刚体动力学、来自大约 170 个风洞表的空气动力学、标准大气以及两份 NASA 技术备忘录中描述的控制面混合器。 从仅重力健全性检查到十秒闭环飞行，八种物理场景对结果进行评分。 没有模型能解决这个问题。 这是边界分开的地方：

Terra 在没有阅读飞行手册的情况下运送了飞行器。 它提取 NASA 备忘录的一次尝试在 3.5 分钟失败了，并且再也没有尝试过 - 因此它发明了控制混合器，从场景表中逆向工程收益。 它完成了四次完整的飞行，并且从未查看过返回代码；它自己的日志显示控制面与规范规定值相差十一度，未注明。 同类中最便宜的尝试，最差的全程飞行。

索尔阅读了所有内容并验证了各个部分。 它在第三分钟提取了两份备忘录，将其空气动力学构建为所提供表格的解释器，并将它们锁定在数据文件中嵌入的 NASA 的 24 个检查案例中 - 所有 24 个案例均在该组中最快运行的第 27 分钟通过。 它从未验证过的是一条轨迹：它的荷兰滚以 48 度的俯冲结束于海平面以下，其结论是“舵的行为似乎是正确的”。

卢娜从未让飞机飞过。 它在 80 分钟内解决了 23 次编译错误，然后通过将飞行器的垂直空气动力和俯仰扭矩重新连接到零来解决它，并且在运输场景中它只运行了十分之一秒。 它的承诺飞行器下降而不旋转：姿态四元数永远不会移动。 两个半小时，544 次工具调用，垫底。

《神鬼寓言》在写一行之前花了三分之一的时间来阅读。 规格、表格、两份备忘录——它将 PDF 页面渲染为图像来解决一个模糊的常数——然后编写了 16 个文件，这些文件在第一次尝试时编译，运行所有八个场景，并针对它能找到的每一个神谕以伪造电池结束。 如果存在外部参考，则它在队列中得分最高；没有人这么做的地方，它就和其他人一起倒下了。

05·判决结果

判决。

关于展示的能力——智能体可以解决的问题集的比例——答案并不接近。 Anthropic 的寓言在该研究中取得了最高的难度加权分数，是唯一一个横扫四个核心问题的所有 12 项试验的模型，并且在未解决的 HL-20 上处于领先地位 - 在存在外部参考的每个评分测试中都获得最高分。 定罪费用为：每次审判 9.60 美元，研究费用 124.76 美元，是 GPT 的三到八倍。

OpenAI 的 GPT 5.6 系列拥有价值前沿。 Sol 在性能上排名第二，价格仅为《神鬼寓言》的五分之一，并在此过程中建立了一些该研究中最好的独立验证。 Terra 是获得可信分数的最便宜、最快的途径，通过削减利润来实现这一目标。 Luna 在各个方面都落后：得分最后，成本第二高，是其兄弟姐妹挂钟的两倍。

所以：如果“最好”意味着每美元拥有最多的物理特性，那么它就是 sol。 如果“最佳”意味着所承诺的模型实际上正确的概率最高（标准物理人工智能最终会回答），那么它就是克劳德寓言 5。 但请注意该表的每一行都有哪些共同点。 每个模型都使用相同的工具来达到这些数字：一个为它提供编译器反馈的工具、模拟工具和一个拒绝被仅仅运行的代码所吸引的分级器。

06·更大的杠杆

安全带如何改变事物。

上述所有内容都改变了模型并保持了安全带静止，该实验的诚实总结比围绕前沿版本的营销所暗示的要小：选择最好的模型而不是最差的模型值得 0.162 权重点，即 0.727 到 0.889。 我们的配套研究进行了逆向实验——模型固定，工具不同——通过 Dyad AI 工具和库存通用编码代理：Claude Code，针对相同的密封问题发送相同的前沿模型，并提供相同的定制文档和 Dyad 编译工具。

这个逆实验将分数提高了更多。 相同的模型，相同的问题，几乎相同的支出：库存代理中的 0.533，Dyad 工具中的 0.899 - 0.366 点的差距，是上述最佳和最差前沿模型之间的 0.162 的两倍多。 股票代理在风格点上也没有输：在相对论动力学问题上，它在每次试验中得分为零。 简单地说：交换模型会改变谁获胜；交换线束会改变物理原理是否正确。

两名特工的评分相同——每个人提交的物理模型都经过模拟，并与双方都看不到的密封参考轨迹进行比较。 不同之处在于每个安全带在评分前强制执行的内容。 通用编码代理也可以推导方程和行为，甚至可以验证——没有什么可以阻止它，但也没有什么可以让它这样做。

Dyad 线束专门用于指导法学硕士，它所涵盖的物理建模的理想路径。 验证是通过构建发生的事情。 这就是“我的代码编译”和“我的物理在与求解器接触后幸存下来”之间的区别，没有任何模型质量可以替代它。

07 · 结论

结论。

1. 《神鬼寓言》展示了最广泛的功能。 研究中难度加权得分最高（0.889），唯一一次彻底解决四个核心问题，并且在未解决的 HL-20 上取得最好成绩——在存在外部参考的情况下领先于每项评分测试。 如果要求模型的物理性能正确，那么《神鬼寓言》就是值得购买的模型。

2. GPT 5.6 Sol 在价值上获胜。 第二名是 0.814，一次试用价格为 1.74 美元，大约是 Fable 价格的五分之一，具有该研究中一些最好的独立验证习惯。 对于大部分日常建模工作，Sol 是理性默认值。

3. 安全带提供了很大的杠杆作用。 这里最好和最差前沿模型之间的差距是 0.162 个加权点；线束之间的间隙是其两倍多。 该观点最尖锐的版本是：相同的前沿模型在 Dyad 安全带中得分为 0.899，在股票编码代理中得分为 0.533。 交换前沿模型会使排名改变十分之一点；更换仪器会改变物理学是否正确。 首先选择安全带，然后选择您能负担得起的最佳型号。
